\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فارغ} \fa{التحصیل} (fâregh ot-tahsil)}{فارغ التحصیل (fâregh ot-tahsil)}]{\fa{فارغ} \fa{التحصیل} (fâregh ot-tahsil) — a graduate}

\label{lesson:FA-C403-faregh-ot-tahsil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a thesis, then the Persian for a lecture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فارغ} \fa{التحصیل}}
\textbf{\fa{فارغ} \fa{التحصیل}} (\emph{fâregh ot-tahsil}) — \textquotedblleft{}a graduate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{سال} \fa{گذشته} \fa{فارغ} \fa{التحصیل} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u sâl-e gozashte fâregh ot-tahsil shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He graduated last year.
\end{quote}

An Arabic phrase, literally \textquotedblleft{}free of study\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Fâregh ot-tahsil shodan} — to graduate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{فارغ} \fa{التحصیل}} is usually traced to the Arabic phrase \emph{fārigh al-taḥṣīl}, \textquotedblleft{}free of study\textquotedblright{}: \emph{fārigh} \textquotedblleft{}free, done\textquotedblright{} + \emph{al-} \textquotedblleft{}the\textquotedblright{} + \emph{taḥṣīl} \textquotedblleft{}study\textquotedblright{}. A graduate has finished studying.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fâregh ot-tahsil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fâregh ot-tahsil}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a thesis, then the Persian for a lecture, then say \emph{fâregh ot-tahsil} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تحصیلات} (tahsilât)}{تحصیلات (tahsilât)}]{\fa{تحصیلات} (tahsilât) — education, schooling}

\label{lesson:FA-C403-tahsilat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a lecture, then the Persian for a graduate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تحصیلات}}
\textbf{\fa{تحصیلات}} (\emph{tahsilât}) — \textquotedblleft{}education, schooling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{تحصیلات} \fa{دانشگاهی} \fa{ندارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedaram tahsilât-e dâneshgâhi nadârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father does not have a university education.
\end{quote}

The Arabic-style plural of \emph{tahsil} \textquotedblleft{}study\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تحصیلات}} is the Arabic-style plural of \emph{tahsil} \textquotedblleft{}study\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{taḥṣīl} \textquotedblleft{}obtaining, acquiring\textquotedblright{}: education is what you have acquired.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ارائه} \fa{دادن} (erâ'e dâdan)}{ارائه دادن (erâ'e dâdan)}]{\fa{ارائه} \fa{دادن} (erâ'e dâdan) — to present, to submit}

\label{lesson:FA-C403-erae-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a graduate, then the Persian for education.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ارائه} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{ارائه} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{erâ'e dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to present, to submit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هر} \fa{دانشجو} \fa{باید} \fa{یک} \fa{مقاله} \fa{ارائه} \fa{دهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{har dâneshju bâyad yek maqâle erâ'e dahad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every student must present a paper.
\end{quote}

\emph{Erâ'e} \textquotedblleft{}presentation\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâdan} (stem \emph{deh-}). Formal; spelled with \fa{ئ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ارائه}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{irā'a} \textquotedblleft{}showing\textquotedblright{}; with \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to PIE \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-}, it means to put something before people.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{erâ'e dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{erâ'e dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a graduate, then the Persian for education, then say \emph{erâ'e dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لیسانس} (lisâns)}{لیسانس (lisâns)}]{\fa{لیسانس} (lisâns) — a bachelor's degree}

\label{lesson:FA-C403-lisans}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for education, then the Persian for to present.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لیسانس}}
\textbf{\fa{لیسانس}} (\emph{lisâns}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bachelor's degree\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{لیسانس} \fa{زبان} \fa{انگلیسی} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u lisâns-e zabân-e engelisi dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She has a bachelor's degree in English.
\end{quote}

A French loan; the official term is \emph{kârshenâsi}. \emph{Fowq-e lisâns} — a master's degree.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{لیسانس}} is usually traced to French \emph{licence}, a university degree, from Latin \emph{licentia} \textquotedblleft{}freedom, leave\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دکترا} (doktorâ)}{دکترا (doktorâ)}]{\fa{دکترا} (doktorâ) — a doctorate, a PhD}

\label{lesson:FA-C403-doktora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to present, then the Persian for a bachelor's degree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دکترا}}
\textbf{\fa{دکترا}} (\emph{doktorâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a doctorate, a PhD\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{عمویم} \fa{دکترای} \fa{شیمی} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'amuyam doktorâ-ye shimi dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle has a doctorate in chemistry.
\end{quote}

\emph{Doktorâ gereftan} — to get a PhD.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{دکترا}} is usually traced to French \emph{doctorat} \textquotedblleft{}doctorate\textquotedblright{}, built on Latin \emph{doctor} \textquotedblleft{}teacher\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{docere} \textquotedblleft{}to teach\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
